transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. As part of our normal operating review, I want to understand what's been breaking down in the handoffs between Client Operations and Implementation. Lina, Omar — you two currently share responsibility for handling client escalations, and I know several recent handoffs have led to disagreements about who communicates with the client and who owns the internal follow-up. Before I finalize any changes to the process, I'd like each of you to describe what arrangement would make the handoff genuinely workable. Let's start with you, Lina — what would you need in terms of clarity or structure?

transcript.text: Before the previous department head left, Omar and I had an informal agreement that I would own client-facing escalation communication and Omar would own internal root-cause follow-up for six weeks. That six-week period has passed, and the agreement was never added to the operating documentation. I think that split actually worked well when we followed it, but without it being documented, the clarity broke down over time.

transcript.text: Thanks, Lina. I agree that the split you described — you owning client-facing communication and me owning internal root-cause follow-up — worked well in practice. My view is that we should formalize that division in the operating documentation so it doesn't decay again. Beyond that, I do have a constraint I need to flag for the group: I'm currently managing some burnout symptoms, and for the next four weeks I can only reliably join a coordination meeting on Tuesdays at 14:00. I also need handoff details in writing before that meeting so I can prepare properly. If we can build the recurring coordination around that window and ensure details come to me in writing ahead of time, I think the handoff arrangement can work well for everyone.
